pr_title: Force updates for ZHA light group entity members
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR forces updates for entities that are used to derive state for ZHA light group entities. There are some manufacturers who do not follow the ZCL specification when lights are added and commanded by a group. They stop reporting attribute changes and this causes the states to be incorrect. Now we force network reads to prevent this from happening.

issue_context.title: Issues with state updates when controlling multiple lights with ZHA
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
When turning on/off multiple lights connected through the ZHA integration at the same time not all lights update their state immediately. It can take several minutes for the correct state to show. 

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.111.2
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unknown
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Supervised
- Integration causing this issue: zha / Zigbee Home Automation
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zha/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
  - platform: group
    name: woonkamer_vloer_ha_group
    entities:
      - light.woonkamer_boekenkast
      - light.woonkamer_trap
      - light.woonkamer_raam_tuin
      - light.woonkamer_raam_voor
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->


## Additional information
I set up the ZHA integration, using a Conbee 2 stick connected to a Raspberry Pi 4. The relevant part of my setup are four Hue light bulbs connected using ZHA. Controlling these lights individually works perfectly every single time, but I have two issues when controlling all four at the same time.

1. If I configure a group in ZHA containing all four lights, I can control them perfectly using the group entity. However, if I do so the state of the individual lights can take minutes to update. I would expect this to be instant. 
The same thing happens if I create three groups in ZHA; one with all four lights and two groups of two lights each. If I turn on the group with four lights most of the time one of the smaller groups will show the correct state immediately, and the other one will take several minutes to update. 
2. As a workaround I tried to create a light group in Home Assistant (see the configuration snippet I included). This works _most of the time_, but about 20-25% of the time one or two of the lights are turned on or off like intended, but don't immediately update their state in Home Assistant.
comments:
I have the exact same issue having created a light group to control 2 ESP Home Light entities.
Around 25% of the time the 2 entities I am trying to connect are not commanded in sync. There also is a short flicker of both child entities when modifying the group brightness. It does not occur every time. Interestingly, this bug only occurs when controlling child entities through the light group entity. When controlling each child entity individually, they both react as expected.
Hue lights are not reporting their state and instead are polled. For HUE lights there's going to be a delay until their state gets in sync again.
as for controlling the lights as a group, you would be better of creating a zigbee group and adding light to the group instead of using the light_group integration

The problem is that I have lights that I want to control both individually and as a group. In those cases whichever method I choose, either the individual light state or the group state will lag behind. 
I'm not familiar with the ZHA code, but would it be feasible to improve this behaviour along the following lines?

- ZHA knows which lights are part of a Zigbee group; so the internal state for the group could be updated immediately if a single light is changed 
- Same for the other way around: if a state change for a group containing multiple lights is requested the state of the individual lights is updated too
- If some of the lights ignore the Zigbee message to change state the incorrect will be updated by the normal polling mechanism

The end result is the same, but the correct state would be shown right away. If you have pointers for where to get started on this I'm happy to have a look myself, but I'm not really familiar with the Home Assistant codebase.

You’re assuming that the state change is actually performed by the lights if you do this. There are plenty of cases where messages could drop and by doing this you also cause a desync in states. The way it is now ensures that after the polling delay that the state is always accurate. This only affects lights that don’t report their state right? For lights that follow the spec and do properly report their state there is no lag in the group entities state that I have seen.

I'd have to do a bit more testing, I'll see if I can do so tomorrow. From what I've seen so far both Hue and Innr lights in my setup don't report their state immediately, I also have a set of Ikea lights that I can try this with.
When controlling individual lights state should be updated immediately, as long as device acknowledges the request

> For lights that follow the spec and do properly report their state there is no lag in the group entities state that I have seen.

I just did some testing with three Zigbee/ZHA groups:
- One consisting of Hue bulbs
- One consisting of Innr bulbs
- One consisting of Ikea Tradfri bulbs

None of these lights appears to send a state report when turned on or off via a group. The reverse _does_ work; when changing an individual bulb the ZHA group state is updated immediately (or at least as soon as the light acknowledges executing the command), this works across all three brands I tested. So unless I'm missing something really obvious here it seems like I'll have to rely on Home Assistant's generic light groups instead of Zigbee/ZHA groups if I want to control lights both individually and separately.
yeah, Ikea doesn't seem to send attr report when commanded through group. need to debug it.
Still thinking about how to handle this. We have some ideas. Hope to have something implemented for .114
What is the status on this one. I still have a lot off problems with ZHA group states not updating 😞

I'm also still experiencing this issue. It causes my toggles to not work properly since after the off-toggle, some entities and hence the group still report the on state. I then need to do two additional toggles to turn the group back on.

review_comments: The light component shouldn't be used from a platform. We should use the dispatch helper instead to signal the relevant entities.
This is where I 🤷🏻‍♂️ Tell me what u want us to do and I’ll do i
Sometimes I wish HA had a `f"{domain}. update_state"` service. I don't quite understand ~~understand~~(happy Saturday everyone) why this should be any different from `light.turn_on` service

Here's an example of how to use the dispatch helper:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/650d61e4f3007d1f7d456713d43fbc30b7396ce6/homeassistant/components/tuya/__init__.py#L160

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/650d61e4f3007d1f7d456713d43fbc30b7396ce6/homeassistant/components/tuya/__init__.py#L212-L216

In our case we can simply let the light entities that  should be targeted by the forced update subscribe to a common force update signal string. Those entities subscribe in `async_added_to_hass` with the `async_get_state` method as target callback, or if needed an intermediate method.

Yeah ZHA uses this everywhere... I’m thinking of how to do this efficiently. The problem we have here is this is a group entity and the entities that make up the group don’t know anything about the group or the group entity. They don’t even know they’re in the group. But the group entity does have the info it needs. We also can’t do anything with entity Id based signals because the entity id can be changed. That’s why I chose to do this like this.

I could signal the group object and then move this code to the ZHAGroup so that it isn’t in light.py would that solve your concern with the platform issue?
@MartinHjelmare how's this: https://github.com/dmulcahey/home-assistant/commit/ca37afa12583d5f1f154c5fcf207460103c95dc9 If that's good I'll PR the update
